evaluation_epoch: Midpoint of each 24-hour observation day, GPST calendar labels. Both stations have identical published velocities, so the expected baseline is epoch-invariant.
antenna_epoch_rule: A published coordinate describes the antenna that was on the monument when the data behind it was collected. A station whose antenna changed after the coordinate epoch is therefore describing a configuration the observations are not of, and NGS states such a change moves the coordinate by a few mm to several cm. Every station whose coordinate is compared against must carry one antenna, installed on or before reference_epoch and never removed. GODS fails this rule and is retained unjudged as the counter-case.

GODS.antenna_epoch_exempt: Counter-case, not a reference. Its antenna changed on 2020-09-03, after the 2020.0 coordinate epoch, which is the effect this dataset demonstrates. The accuracy criterion is never judged on it, and the guard checks that this exemption is still earned.

tolerance_status: tolerance_m is the REPORTED published-coordinate comparison, not a criterion. It stays at the 1 mm conservative reading of specs/20 section 6 printed-source precision so the number keeps its meaning across the change, but nothing fails on it: specs/22 section 5.4 measured the reference's own uncertainty at roughly 5 mm per component on fourteen clean pairs.
selection: Two nonzero short baselines from one base at the same NASA site, authoritative NGS ITRF2020 ARP coordinates and velocities, and publicly reusable NOAA observations. GODE is the accuracy case: its antenna was installed 2013-01-30 and never removed, so the published coordinate and the observations describe the same instrument. GODS is the counter-case: its antenna changed on 2020-09-03, after the 2020.0 coordinate epoch. The pair was found by screening all 2886 CORS station logs, not chosen after solving; every same-type candidate longer than 4 km errs by 13 to 47 mm under this processing configuration, which is why the site did not change. No epochs or days were selected to meet the threshold.

recorded_solution.note: The frozen GODN-GODS day-001 solution from the original experiment. It is history, not expected truth, and it is retained because it is the counter-case's evidence: it shows the 6 to 7 mm north that GODS's post-epoch antenna change accounts for. Its case name predates the GODE/GODS naming and is kept so the bytes and observed-results.json stay in step.

criterion: Loop closure over the GODN-GODE-GODS triangle and robust six-hour sub-session repeatability, both at 2 mm per component. Maintainer's decision of 24 September 2026: GNSS is judged on what this project controls. The published-coordinate comparison is reported and no longer judged, because fourteen independent clean pairs put the reference's own spread at about 5 mm while this estimator repeats to well under one -- see specs/22 section 5.4 and specs/20 section 6.
